title: Winey Chewy Polish Hake Pilaf
description: A pescatarian-friendly Polish dish featuring hake fillets, cooked in a flavorful wine sauce and served with a side of chewy starch. This dish is perfect for a sick day, as it's easy to digest and requires minimal cooking effort.
instructions: Heat a large non-stick iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon of butter and melt it, then add the hake fillets and cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown.

Remove the hake from the pan and set it aside to rest. In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter and melt it over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 3-4 minutes, until softened.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional minute, until fragrant.
Add the white wine to the pan and stir to deglaze the bottom, scraping up any browned bits. Bring the wine to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes, until reduced by half.
Add the caraway seeds and flour to the pan and stir to combine. Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the mixture forms a smooth paste.
Gradually add the chicken broth to the pan, whisking continuously to avoid lumps. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Add the cooked hake back to the pan and toss to coat with the sauce. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
To serve, divide the cooked rice among four plates, then top each plate with a hake fillet and spoon some of the sauce over the top. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve hot.
If desired, drizzle a tablespoon of white vinegar over the dish for added brightness.
